security.title: PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Fixes Coming November 19
security.summary: The maintainers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday issued an advisory announcing an upcoming security release that addresses critical flaws. The release is scheduled for November 19, 2026, between 2 and 2:30 p.m. UTC. "These releases are part of PHP's regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions," the maintainers said.

security.summary: A flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 support can allow an attacker to run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled, without needing to log in. The decade-old flaw, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed "nginx2root," has been present in NGINX's open-source code since version 1.9.5, released on September 22, 2015.
